title: Fonctions L / Équation fonctionnelle des fonctions L (cas géométrique) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This is a short handwritten fragment ending a step in a proof. It reads: 'On voit donc que c) est ramené (modulo un signe) au cas de b), donc à déterminer χ^G(E_y). Or cette détermination est faite en utilisant les représentations d'Artin ----'.

The folder is about the functional equation of L-functions in the geometric case. The context is therefore almost certainly the Grothendieck–Ogg–Shafarevich computation of Euler–Poincaré characteristics on a curve.

In modern terms the argument would run as follows. A constructible sheaf (or representation) on a curve is trivialised on a finite Galois cover Y→X with group G. Global Euler characteristics are then computed G-equivariantly. Here χ^G denotes an Euler characteristic taken in a Grothendieck group of G-modules (projective modules or the representation ring). E_y is the fibre, or local contribution, at a point y of the cover.

The 'cases' a), b), c) are presumably cases of a dévissage. Case c) is reduced, up to a sign, to case b). Case b) in turn requires computing the local equivariant term χ^G(E_y) at a ramified point.

This local term is identified with the Artin representation (equivalently the Swan representation) of the inertia/decomposition group at y. Its character is a_G(s) = -i_G(s) for s ≠ 1, and the trivial-character value is fixed by the sum over G being 0. Pairing with the coefficient representation yields the Artin/Swan conductor. This is exactly the mechanism in Grothendieck's proof of the Euler–Poincaré formula (SGA 5, exp. X), as exposed by Raynaud (Séminaire Bourbaki n°286).

The page breaks off with a dash, signalling that the details are known or to be filled in.

The neighbouring sheets are typed Bourbaki drafts (Algèbre commutative ch. VII, 'Diviseurs', §4: lattices, Prop. 19, Lemma 4, the norm map N : D(B)→D(A), n°392). Grothendieck reused them as scrap paper; they have no mathematical connection to this page.
errors: No mathematical error can be assessed; the argument is only sketched. The 'modulo un signe' indicates a sign bookkeeping issue left unchecked here, which is standard (alternating sum and Artin character sign conventions).

deep.surprise_reason: This is a five-line transitional fragment pointing to the standard use of Artin representations in the Grothendieck–Ogg–Shafarevich Euler characteristic computation. That use is well documented in SGA 5 and in Raynaud's Bourbaki talk. The only incidental historical detail is that the sheets reuse typed Bourbaki drafts of Commutative Algebra ch. VII.
transcription_corrections: Line 2: the bracketed '[?]' should read '(modulo un signe)' — the phrase 'modulo un signe' is underlined in the manuscript.
The final line ends with 'représentations d'Artin ----', i.e. the text deliberately breaks off; nothing further is written on the page.
Page number 58 appears at bottom left.
